findings.decompiled: mem[ceil32(_ipfs.length) + 224] = mem[160]; idx = 32; while idx < _ipfs.length: mem[idx + ceil32(_ipfs.length) + 224] = mem[idx + 160]; idx = idx + 32
findings.source: ChainLog.sol: ipfs = _ipfs; emit UpdateIPFS(_ipfs); (same shape as setVersion)
findings.issue: The event's string copy is a rotated word loop (first word before the loop, P3/P7) in setIPFS and setSha256sum, while the identical copy in setVersion is printed as a single copy line, so the same source construct reads differently in three sibling functions.
findings.rule: Un-rotate a loop whose pre-header performs the first iteration, then recognise an element-wise memory-to-memory word copy as a copy line.

notes: Small solc-0.6.12 contract (239 lines); all 16 functions reviewed. No source loops; the two whiles are the implicit string copies above. Storage string writes are shown with copy lines, the short-string encoding `2 * len | 256 * mem[160 len 31]`, and the old-tail clear `stor[_11 len -_11 + max(_10, _11)] = 0`, all correct (the old length decode `(256 * (not _3) - 1 & _4) / 2` is solc 0.6's formula). setAddress/removeAddress (keys array with swap-and-pop, positions mapping) and the wards checks follow the source. No semantic error found.
summary: Clean, faithful text without source loops; the only oddity is that one memory string copy is printed as a rotated while in two functions and as a copy line in their sibling.
